facts.fact: AdImpact projects $10.8 billion in total political ad spending for the 2026 midterm elections, according to the page.
facts.quote: AdImpact projects $10.8 billion in political ad spending, with $2.5 billion flowing to connected TV and streaming platforms alone.

facts.fact: AdImpact projects $2.5 billion in political ad spending on connected TV and streaming platforms for 2026.
facts.quote: with $2.5 billion flowing to connected TV and streaming platforms alone.

facts.fact: The page states that 2026 midterm political ad spending is a 20% increase from 2022.
facts.quote: That's a 20% increase from 2022.

facts.fact: According to AdImpact's 2026 projections as summarized by the page, House and Senate races will account for $5 billion combined in spending.
facts.quote: $5 billion combined (nearly half of all spending)

facts.fact: According to AdImpact's 2026 projections as summarized by the page, digital and social political ad spending is projected at $1.9 billion.
facts.quote: $1.9 billion projected

facts.fact: The page states that more than 60% of U.S. households use streaming services as their primary TV source.
facts.quote: More than 60% of U.S. households now use streaming services as their primary TV source.

facts.quote: Traditional TV buys often require $50,000+ commitments.

facts.fact: The page lists prime time 30-second broadcast spots in major markets (New York, LA, Chicago) at $5,000 to $50,000+.
facts.quote: Prime time 30-second spot: $5,000-50,000+

facts.fact: The page lists prime time broadcast spots in mid-size markets at $500 to $5,000.
facts.quote: Prime time: $500-5,000

facts.fact: The page lists prime time broadcast spots in small markets at $100 to $1,000.
facts.quote: Prime time: $100-1,000

facts.fact: The page states cable TV typically costs CPM of $5 to $25 depending on network and market.
facts.quote: CPM (cost per thousand):** $5-25 depending on network and market

facts.fact: The page states cable minimum buys are often $5,000 to $10,000 per month.
facts.quote: Minimum buys:** Often $5,000-10,000 per month

facts.fact: The page states zone targeting on cable adds 10% to 20% to base rates.
facts.quote: Zone targeting:** Adds 10-20% to base rates

facts.fact: The page lists premium CTV inventory on Hulu and Peacock at $25 to $45 CPM.
facts.quote: Premium inventory (Hulu, Peacock):** $25-45 CPM

facts.fact: The page lists FAST channels such as Tubi and Pluto TV at $15 to $25 CPM.

facts.fact: Adwave's self-serve platform starts at $30 a day, according to the page.

facts.quote: Can spend unlimited amounts but cannot coordinate with campaigns

facts.quote: doesn't apply to PACs or issue campaigns.

facts.fact: As an illustrative example, the page says a $500 CTV campaign at $25 CPM delivers 20,000 ad views to targeted voters.
facts.quote: A $500 CTV campaign at $25 CPM delivers 20,000 ad views to targeted voters.

facts.fact: As an illustrative example, the page says a $2,000 CTV spend by a school board candidate can reach 80,000+ targeted impressions in their district.
facts.quote: A school board candidate spending $2,000 on CTV can reach 80,000+ targeted impressions in their district

facts.fact: The Adwave guide suggests that for competitive races, TV/CTV advertising should be 40-60% of the media budget.
facts.quote: TV/CTV advertising: 40-60% of media budget

facts.fact: The Adwave guide suggests digital/social should be 20-30% of the media budget for competitive races.
facts.quote: Digital/social: 20-30%

facts.fact: The Adwave guide suggests mail should be 10-20% of the media budget for competitive races.
The Adwave guide suggests field/other should be 10-15% of the media budget for competitive races.
facts.quote: Field/other: 10-15%

facts.fact: Within TV spending, the Adwave guide suggests CTV/streaming should be 50-70% for most down-ballot races.
facts.quote: CTV/streaming: 50-70% (for most down-ballot races)

facts.fact: Within TV spending, the Adwave guide suggests broadcast should be 20-40% if the budget allows.
facts.quote: Broadcast: 20-40% (if budget allows)

facts.fact: Within TV spending, the Adwave guide suggests cable should be 10-20%, noting its declining importance.
facts.quote: Cable: 10-20% (declining importance)

facts.fact: The Adwave guide states that for races under $50,000 total budget, CTV often makes more sense than broadcast due to lower minimums and better targeting.
facts.quote: For races under $50,000 total budget, CTV often makes more sense than broadcast due to lower minimums and better targeting.

facts.fact: The Adwave guide gives a production cost range of $10,000 to $100,000+ for professional political TV ad shoots.
facts.quote: Production options range from professional shoots ($10,000-100,000+)

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends issue education and early awareness 6-12 months before election day.
facts.quote: 6-12 months out** - Issue education and early awareness

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends introduction and platform communication 3-6 months before election day.
facts.quote: 3-6 months out** - Introduction and platform communication

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends persuasion messaging and contrast advertising 1-3 months before election day.
facts.quote: 1-3 months out** - Persuasion messaging and contrast advertising

facts.fact: The Adwave guide recommends saturation and turnout advertising in the final 30 days before election day.
facts.quote: Final 30 days** - Saturation and turnout

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that broadcast TV political advertising ranges from $100 to $50,000+ per spot, depending on market size and timing.
facts.quote: Broadcast TV ranges from $100 to $50,000+ per spot depending on market size and timing.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that CTV/streaming political advertising typically costs $15-45 CPM.
facts.quote: CTV/streaming advertising typically costs $15-45 CPM.

facts.quote: Campaigns can start CTV advertising for as little as $50 through self-serve platforms

facts.fact: Adwave's guide gives an example that a school board candidate can run targeted streaming TV ads to their district for $500-2,000.
facts.quote: A school board candidate can run targeted streaming TV ads to their district for $500-2,000

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that many campaigns start with $500-1,000 test campaigns to validate targeting before scaling.
facts.quote: Many campaigns start with $500-1,000 test campaigns to validate targeting before scaling.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that issue campaigns often begin 6-12 months before elections.
facts.quote: Issue campaigns often begin 6-12 months before elections.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that candidate campaigns typically start TV advertising 3-6 months out, intensifying in the final 60-90 days.
facts.quote: Candidate campaigns typically start 3-6 months out for introduction and platform messaging, intensifying in the final 60-90 days.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that federal candidate political TV ads must include an "I approve this message" statement.
facts.quote: Federal candidate ads must include "I approve this message" statements.

facts.fact: Adwave's guide states that all political ads must identify who paid for them.
facts.quote: All political ads must identify who paid for them.
